reviewerRole: Separate trusted evaluator agent; not the importer author. Production accounting source was reviewed read-only.
scope: stale copied journals and revision history
expired prepared recovery and concurrent writer fencing

historicalFindings.problem: An expired prepared receipt that had not reached the ledger could neither retry nor permit its next reviewed revision.
historicalFindings.initialEvidence: Independently reproduced with temporary synthetic prepared-state injection: retry rejected expired, next revision rejected previous-prepared, and 1000000 microdollars remained held.
historicalFindings.correction: Explicit reviewed expiry recovery anchors the receipt, writes a CAS recovery tombstone without releasing the hold, then rejects the old prepared entry. A new reviewed contiguous revision can reconcile.
historicalFindings.finalEvidence: Independent expiry/fencing control passes; author child-process controls cover crashes after anchor and recovery tombstone.

historicalFindings.problem: An already-applied duplicate returned before checking immutable reservation binding.
historicalFindings.initialEvidence: Read-only source finding; no initial financial mutation or spending bypass claimed.
historicalFindings.correction: Immutable ledger binding is validated before duplicate return. Journal and ledger identities are paired durably. Historical duplicates preserve current higher totals.
historicalFindings.finalEvidence: Independent cross-ledger control and combined historical-duplicate control pass.

historicalFindings.problem: A replacement importer journal lacked prior revision and cumulative CPU history.
historicalFindings.initialEvidence: Read-only source finding: history existed only in the caller-selected importer database.
historicalFindings.correction: Each durable ledger binds one journal identity, and each journal binds its ledger identity.
historicalFindings.finalEvidence: Independent fresh-journal and different-ledger controls reject before changing money.

historicalFindings.problem: An old copy of the same logical journal could retain its UUID while omitting newer revision/CPU history.
historicalFindings.initialEvidence: Read-only design finding acknowledged by the author; not a demonstrated USD-cap bypass.
historicalFindings.correction: Each prepared receipt is anchored in the ledger before reconciliation. Missing, conflicting or skipped anchored revisions fail closed.
historicalFindings.finalEvidence: Independent stale-copy control retains the newer ledger state; author controls cover copies before the first receipt and after an earlier revision.

historicalFindings.problem: Expired recovery could reread newer ledger evidence after a CAS race and attempt to replace a newer applied receipt with an old tombstone.
historicalFindings.initialEvidence: Read-only interleaving finding. The author added the revision guard before the independent interleaving first executed; no pre-fix runtime reproduction is claimed.
historicalFindings.correction: Receipt reconciliation and recovery check expectedAccountingReceiptDigest inside the same ledger transaction as evidence CAS and money changes.
historicalFindings.finalEvidence: Independent controlled interleaving applies the old receipt and a newer revision during recovery. Old recovery receives accounting_history_conflict; the newer evidence digest, 200000-microdollar charge, zero hold, and both applied journal rows remain intact.

limitations: Receipt consistency is not provider authenticity. Accepted digests and expected bindings must come from independent trusted evidence ingestion; authenticityVerified remains false.
Real operation inventory, remote cleanup and measured billing remain unverified by these tests.
Low-level ledger reconciliation remains a trusted interface; it does not itself impose all receipt CPU/history policy.
Privileged rollback or coordinated editing of both databases is outside these consistency controls; matched SQLite-consistent backups are required.
Process-exit and controlled interleaving tests are bounded durability evidence, not exhaustive crash or hardware-failure proof.
This review made no changes to provider, repair, executor, fixture or evaluator-oracle logic.
